# Asana

`asana` reads the Asana of whoever connected it on nanou.ai → Connectors → Asana. Output is JSON. When several people connected it, add `--owner <first name>`; use the asker's own unless they name someone else.

Read:

- `asana tasks`: their open tasks; `asana tasks --project 'Roadmap'`, `--all` for completed too
- `asana task <gid>`: notes, subtasks, comments
- `asana search 'release notes'`, `asana projects --search web`
- `asana inbox --since 1d`: their Asana inbox, rebuilt (Asana's API has no inbox): what others did on tasks they follow, with comments that @mention them flagged `mentionsYou`. Use it for "what's new in Asana", "anything for me in Asana" and morning briefings; lead with mentions and tasks assigned to them, then group the rest by task. It can't see what they already read or archived in Asana.
- Task status: besides `done` (the completed checkbox), tasks show `section` (board column) and `status` (every field named like Status, e.g. `Dev Status: 🎉 Done · Oak Status: Open`). Report them as they are; don't call a task done unless `done` is true, and when the fields disagree, say so (e.g. "dev says done, audit still open").

Change (each one gets an approval card; run it as is, without `--readonly`):

- `asana comment <gid> --text "..."`
- `asana create --name "..." [--project ...] [--assignee me|<email>] [--due YYYY-MM-DD] [--notes ...]`
- `asana update <gid> [--name ...] [--due ...] [--assignee ...] [--notes ...]`
- `asana complete <gid>`, `asana reopen <gid>`

Comments read like the person wrote them: short and plain, no headers or bold.

## Rules

- If `asana` says it isn't connected, send them to nanou.ai → Connectors → Asana. Never ask for a token in chat.
- Never touch `~/.config/connectors/asana` (the tokens live there; it's blocked).
- Work content may be confidential: summarize rather than paste long threads, and don't copy it into family lists or notes unless they ask.
